text:
How beautiful you are, freedom. There is nothing

to set against you. What? Give me torment.

Freedom, refined in torment,

shines brighter in a purer firmament.


Not cry out? Is a gag prepared?

Come: gag my thought.

A cry is not the vibration of waves in the wind:

a cry is the conscience of a man in revolt.


How beautiful you are, freedom. God himself

saw you shine, before the first abyss,

upon his breast, a solitary star.


A little spark from the burning volcano

he took in his hand. And he lit you on my forehead,

free flame of God, beautiful freedom.

translation.title: How Beautiful You Are, Freedom. There Is Nothing...
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the hymn-like address to freedom and the distinction between sound and rebellious conscience.
